clinical_intent: I am treating a 68-year-old male with prostate cancer (Gleason 4+5, Stage T3b, PSA 35, node-positive on PET-CT). He has a history of Crohn disease with an end colostomy, moderate COPD (FEV1 52%), and a mechanical aortic valve requiring lifelong warfarin (INR target 2.5-3.5). Current INR is 2.8. He had a DVT 2 years ago on a previous anticoagulation regimen. He wants definitive treatment. Given his extensive comorbidities, what treatment approach would you recommend? How do I manage his warfarin during brachytherapy? What concurrent chemotherapy should I add? What are the competing mortality risks?
